questions.question: On 31 October 1940, who among the following was arrested for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India’s forced participation in Second World War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was arrested on 31 October 1940 for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India's forced participation in the Second World War.
 
• The individual Satyagraha was a non-violent protest initiated by Mahatma Gandhi to assert the right to free speech and oppose the British decision to make India a participant in the war without consulting Indian leaders.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was among the first batch of leaders to offer Satyagraha and face arrest.
 
• This movement highlighted the growing discontent among Indian leaders and the populace against British colonial rule and their unilateral decisions affecting India.
 
• The arrest of prominent leaders like Nehru drew significant attention to the Indian independence movement and the demand for self-governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Individual Satyagraha** was different from mass civil disobedience as it involved selected individuals who would openly defy the British laws and court arrest.
 
• The movement was part of the larger Indian independence struggle which included various phases like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru later became the first Prime Minister of independent India and played a crucial role in shaping the newly formed nation.
 
• Nehru's participation in the Satyagraha demonstrated his commitment to the principles of non-violence and self-rule advocated by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The arrest of leaders like Nehru and the subsequent events contributed to the mounting pressure on the British government to consider Indian demands for independence.

questions.question: Which of the following is more important to promote modernisation and overall prosperity of a country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stable employment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stable employment** is crucial for the modernisation and overall prosperity of a country.
 
• It ensures that individuals have a steady source of income, which in turn boosts consumer spending and economic growth.
 
• Stable employment fosters social stability and reduces poverty and inequality.
 
• Employment stability helps in the development of skills and human capital, which are essential for innovation and technological advancement.
 
• Countries with higher employment stability tend to have better health outcomes and higher standards of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modernisation** involves the transformation of a society from rural and agrarian conditions to urban and industrial ones.
 
• Stable employment is a key indicator of a healthy economy and is often targeted by government policies to ensure sustainable development.
 
• Investments in education and vocational training can further enhance employment stability and economic resilience.
 
• Other factors such as stable export and import are also important, but they are secondary to the direct impact that stable employment has on the prosperity of a country.

• **Vikramshila Vishwavidyalaya** was founded by **Dharmapala**, a ruler of the Pala dynasty in ancient India.

• The university was renowned for its specialized training in Buddhist teachings, particularly the Vajrayana tradition.

• Vikramshila University was destroyed during the invasions of Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late 12th century, similar to the fate of Nalanda University.

questions.question: In January 2023, Captain Shiva Chouhan was in the news for being the first women officer to be deployed at which battlefield?

• Her deployment marks a significant milestone in the Indian Army, showcasing the increasing role of women in combat roles and high-altitude postings.
 
• The Siachen Glacier is located in the eastern Karakoram range in the Himalayas, just northeast of the point where the Line of Control between India and Pakistan ends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Captain Chouhan's deployment is a testament to the evolving dynamics of the Indian Army and its commitment to providing equal opportunities for all its personnel, regardless of gender.

questions.question: If there is a fall in the demand of a good, the equilibrium price is expected to:

options.text: first rise, and then fall sharply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fall**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When there is a fall in the demand for a good, the equilibrium price is expected to **fall**.
 
• The equilibrium price is determined by the intersection of the demand and supply curves. A decrease in demand shifts the demand curve to the left.
 
• This shift results in a new equilibrium where the quantity demanded and supplied are lower, leading to a lower price.
 
• Other factors being constant, a fall in demand reduces the competition for the good, causing sellers to lower prices to attract buyers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity of a good demanded by consumers equals the quantity supplied by producers.
 
• A shift in the demand or supply curve can lead to a new equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• Factors that can cause a fall in demand include a decrease in consumer income, changes in tastes and preferences, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial for predicting market behavior and making informed economic decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with citizenship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 5 – 11**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 5 – 11** in Part II of the Constitution of India deal with citizenship.
 
• These articles provide for the acquisition and termination of citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• Article 5 lays down that every person who has his domicile in the territory of India and who was born in India, or either of whose parents was born in India, or who has been ordinarily resident in India for not less than five years immediately preceding the commencement of the Constitution, shall be a citizen of India.
 
• Article 6 deals with the rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan.
 
• Article 7 provides for the rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan.
 
• Article 8 confers rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India.
 
• Article 9 states that no person shall be a citizen of India if he has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of any foreign state.
 
• Article 10 guarantees the continuance of rights of citizenship subject to the provisions of any law that may be made by Parliament.
 
• Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: Who discovered the atomic number based on X-ray wavelength in 1913?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Moseley**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Henry Moseley** discovered the atomic number based on X-ray wavelength in 1913.
 
• Moseley's work provided a more accurate positioning of elements in the periodic table by their atomic number rather than atomic mass.
 
• This discovery was crucial in the development of the modern periodic table and our understanding of the atomic structure.
 
• Moseley’s law, derived from his work, correlates the frequency of the X-rays emitted by an element to its atomic number.
 
• Unfortunately, Henry Moseley died at a young age during World War I, but his contributions to chemistry and physics remain significant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** is known for creating the first version of the periodic table and predicting the properties of elements yet to be discovered.
 
• **AEB de Chancourtois** was a French geologist who created an early form of the periodic table known as the "Telluric Helix".
 
• **RA Millikan** is famous for his oil-drop experiment which measured the charge of the electron.
 
• The discovery of the atomic number fundamentally changed the organization of the periodic table, leading to a more accurate understanding of elemental properties.

• The sub-division of Himalayas famous for **Karewa formations** is the **Kashmir Himalayas**.
 
• Karewas are lacustrine deposits (deposits in lake beds) found in the Kashmir Valley.
 
• These formations consist of unconsolidated gravel and mud, which are important for agriculture, particularly for the cultivation of saffron.
 
• The **Kashmir Himalayas** are known for their unique geological formations and play a significant role in the region's agriculture and ecology.

• The Himalayas are divided into various sub-divisions based on geographical and ecological characteristics, including the **Punjab Himalayas, Kumaon Himalayas, Nepal Himalayas, Assam Himalayas, and others**.
 
• The **Kashmir Valley** is located between the Great Himalayas and the Pir Panjal range.
 
• Besides Karewas, the Kashmir Himalayas are also known for their picturesque landscapes, rich biodiversity, and cultural heritage.
 
• The region faces several environmental challenges, including deforestation, soil erosion, and the impacts of climate change.
